name: Carol's African Restaurant
neighborhoodOrCity: Brooklyn Park / Brooklyn Center line (6940 Brooklyn Blvd.)
whatItIs: Family-owned restaurant serving mostly Liberian food (dried rice, jollof, ginger juice), run by Daniel and Jamecar Killen and named for Carol Gbanjah; also caters.
evidence: CCX Media, July 7, 2026, reports it opened in May 2026 and has steady traffic; Spokesman-Recorder, June 27, 2026, reports a May 9 grand opening drawing 200+. Sources differ on city (Brooklyn Park vs. Brooklyn Center).

name: Milah's Royal Bistro
whatItIs: Liberian and West African food; founder Milah Kai, a native of Liberia, per a menu directory.
evidence: Named as a Liberian-owned restaurant in CCX Media's July 2025 Independence Day business story and as part of Brooklyn Park's African food cluster in Hoodline, June 2026. No own website found; hours not confirmed.

name: Christina's Child Care Center
whatItIs: Child care center for ages 6 weeks to 13 years, started by Liberian immigrant Ophelia Zeogar in her basement; assistant director Christina Fraser.
evidence: CCX Media, July 2025, filmed the center operating and said it had been in the family for 19 years. No own website found.

name: Prestigious Care Homes
whatItIs: Home health care business run by Marie Dweh, co-founder of We Are Liberian.
evidence: Named in CCX Media, July 2025, as Dweh's home healthcare service; no own page with current operation was opened.

name: Cavalla Travel & Tours
neighborhoodOrCity: Brooklyn Center (Shingle Creek Center, 6044 Shingle Creek Pkwy.)
whatItIs: Travel agency specializing in Africa, with luggage and travel accessories; owner Jannie Seibure, a native of Liberia.
evidence: CCX Media, June 27, 2024, reported the new storefront opening; St. Paul Area Chamber directory lists the business, undated. No 2025-2026 sign of operation was opened.

name: Shingle Creek Center (Ignite Business Women Investment Group)
whatItIs: 18-storefront strip mall bought in October 2023 by a cooperative of Black immigrant businesswomen, mostly from Liberia, Nigeria and Somalia.
evidence: Next City, Feb. 20, 2024, describes the purchase. ACER's site (checked Oct. 2026) lists Shingle Creek Center items but undated. Current tenants not confirmed.

name: Jambo Africa
whatItIs: Restaurant and nightclub serving Nigerian, Kenyan and Liberian food; hosts Liberian Independence Day and IgboFest events. Owned by AWC Holdings LLC; ownership origin not stated.
evidence: CCX Media, Aug. 11, 2026, reports the current location operating and city approval (July 27, 2026) to build a larger site at 6500 Camden Ave. N.

name: Value Foods Corp. (Value Foods African Market)
whatItIs: African market and restaurant; Liberian ownership not confirmed.
evidence: Own site carries a 2026 copyright and hiring form; Hoodline, June 2026, names Value Foods African Market among Brooklyn Park's African food businesses. Hours not shown.

name: Waterside Market
whatItIs: African market selling cooked and uncooked West African food; Liberian ownership not confirmed.
evidence: Only an aggregated listing was opened; no dated sign of operation.

name: African Foods & Gifts
whatItIs: Deli and store serving West African dishes such as pepper soup, collard greens and cassava leaf; owner Marlene Nah.
evidence: CCX Media, Feb. 15, 2022; no 2025-2026 sign found. The article links the food to Liberia but does not state the owner's origin.

name: 3D's African Kitchen
whatItIs: Restaurant specializing in Nigerian and Liberian dishes; owner Kafayat Abodunrin came from Nigeria.
evidence: CCX Media, April 25, 2024, reported its opening; no later sign found. Not Liberian-owned; listed for its Liberian menu.

name: Mama Ti's
whatItIs: Restaurant serving Liberian home cooking from proprietor Kellita Whisnant's mother's recipes.
evidence: Food Republic, 2014 (updated 2015), described business falling during the Ebola scare; no current sign found.

name: African International Market and Grill
neighborhoodOrCity: Brooklyn Park / Brooklyn Center (Zane Avenue corridor)
whatItIs: African market and grill where chef Waquina Blay said many Liberians worked.
evidence: CCX Media, March 12, 2018; no current sign found.

name: Organization of Liberians in Minnesota (OLM) / Liberian Community Center
whatItIs: Nonprofit community center with senior, youth and community programs; rental hall income noted in 2021.
evidence: Own site lists weekday hours (10 a.m. to 5 p.m.) and July 2026 events; CCX Media, July 2, 2026. Site gives Suite 400 in its footer and Suite 200 on its About page.

name: Liberian Business Association (LIBA / LIBA-Diaspora)
whatItIs: Business association founded 2016 offering technical assistance, QuickBooks training and micro-loans to small, mostly minority-owned businesses; executive director Jackson George (2020).
evidence: Latest opened evidence is a March 2023 Senate handout; CCX Media, Oct. 8, 2020. No 2025-2026 page opened.

name: ACER (African Career, Education & Resource, Inc.)
whatItIs: Nonprofit founded by Wynfred Russell offering small business technical assistance, Main Street grants, housing and civic programs.
evidence: Own site shows 2026 copyright and an October 2026 event.

name: The AfricaPaper
whatItIs: Minnesota community newspaper on African immigrant life; associate editor James Kokulo Fasuekoi is a native of Liberia.
evidence: Site loads, but the newest dated stories seen on the home page are from 2020-2021.

name: CCX Media
neighborhoodOrCity: Brooklyn Park / Brooklyn Center and northwest suburbs (6900 Winnetka Ave. N.)
whatItIs: Community station that regularly covers Liberian organizations, businesses and events. Not Liberian-owned.
